page.headline: Does xs-rs PR #34 beat rsync on csearchv3?
page.intro: The lab is checking whether xs-rs at pull request 34 is faster than its base version and than rsync on the user's csearchv3 tree. One runner, mac, drives the work against apollo, a Linux box. The current experiment runs now until about 9:15pm over 72 samples. Either result leads to the same follow-up test on congress, which checks everyday incremental backups.

runners.title: Mac ↔ apollo: mars's box on Linux

items.asks: On the user's csearchv3 tree, is xs-rs at PR #34 faster than its base and than rsync, fresh, at a no-op and at a 10% update?
items.hypothesis: On csearchv3, xs-rs at PR #34 is at least as fast as its base and faster than rsync at fresh, no-op and a 10% update.
items.why: It runs now on the user's own tree, so it tests whether PR #34 holds up against its base and rsync in the cases that matter.

outcomes.then: IN1-incremental-real-apollo: On congress with 0.1%, 1% and 10% of files edited, the everyday incremental backup, does rsync beat xs?
